subject.title: Feature: Sleep/wait tool — agent can pause execution without burning tokens

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-class core sleep tool, and if so should it be a dedicated gateway resume primitive or a cron-backed session-targeted agentTurn with explicit sandbox policy?
rationale: The request adds a new model-facing core scheduling primitive across agent loop, gateway cron, session resume, interruption, and sandbox boundaries, so automation should not choose the permanent API or security semantics.

options.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
options.body: Accept the feature direction but require a design that resumes the caller session, proves interrupt and restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

options.title: Keep current cron and yield guidance
options.body: Reject a new core tool for now and continue using cron, process completion wakes, and sessions_yield for their documented scopes.

options.title: Narrow to extension API discussion
options.body: Ask for a plugin/runtime extension point first if maintainers want optional scheduling behavior outside the default tool surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a corrected core primitive
recommendation.body: Accept the feature direction but require a design that resumes the caller session, proves interrupt and restart behavior, and keeps sandbox exposure explicit.

likelyOwner.reason: The current central tool, cron, sessions_yield, and sandbox policy blame makes steipete the strongest available routing owner for the product/API decision.
